question: What is the primary clinical purpose of performing needle counts in the operating room?

options.A: To calculate the total cost of consumables used in surgery
options.B: To comply strictly with hospital equipment inventory audits
options.C: To prevent the retention of surgical items inside the patient
options.D: To speed up the surgical team's closure time

explanation: Needle counts are strictly designed to ensure that no sharp foreign bodies are accidentally left inside body cavities during closure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why does a high-pressure surgical emergency in a resource-limited setting make strict adherence to needle counting even more critical?

options.A: Surgeons automatically take over all counting duties during urgent cases
options.B: Emergency procedures never require full instrument trays, making counts obsolete
options.C: Surgical assistants are exempt from documentation rules during night shifts
options.D: Fast-paced environments and fatigue dramatically increase the risk of oversight and retained items

explanation: Fatigue and urgency heighten cognitive distraction, making structured safety barriers like needle counts essential to catch omissions. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which team member is primarily responsible for recording the numbers called out during a surgical count?
explanation: The unsterile circulating nurse documents the figures on a visible board or chart while the scrub nurse handles the items on the sterile table. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: What should the scrub nurse and circulating nurse do together to ensure absolute accuracy during a count?

options.A: Perform separate counts silently to save precious operating time
options.B: Rely entirely on the manufacturer package label without opening packs
options.C: Delegate the final tally to the surgical intern
options.D: Audibly state and visually inspect the items simultaneously

explanation: Synchronized visual inspection and verbal communication prevent miscounting and ensure dual verification. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: When must the initial baseline needle count be performed?

options.A: Immediately after the skin incision has been closed
options.B: Before the surgical procedure begins and packages are opened
options.C: Only if a missing needle is reported mid-surgery
options.D: When the surgeon asks for skin closure material

explanation: Establishing a baseline before the operation starts is mandatory to know the exact number of items introduced to the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: A surgical team is closing the subcutaneous tissue layer of an abdominal wound. What stage of counting should be completed at this exact moment?
explanation: Intraoperative counts are performed as progressive layers (such as deep tissues and subcutaneous layers) are closed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: Where should used surgical needles be safely placed during an operation?

options.A: Directly into the unsterile municipal waste bin
options.B: Inside the general instrument basin for washing
options.C: On a designated magnetic pad, foam block, or suture box
options.D: Loose on the surgical drape near the incision site

explanation: Specialized containment devices keep sharps secure, organized, and easy to visualize during counts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the mandatory action when a surgical needle breaks during use in a deep wound?

options.A: Retrieve and piece together all fragments to verify total recovery
options.B: Assume it will dissolve naturally inside the body tissue
options.C: Discard the largest piece and ignore the tiny tip
options.D: Finish the case quickly without mentioning the break to the team

explanation: All pieces of a broken needle must be accounted for and reassembled to confirm no fragment is left behind in the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the immediate first action when a needle count is found to be incorrect?

options.A: Notify the surgeon and halt wound closure immediately
options.B: Complete the skin closure and document the error later
options.C: Order a replacement tray from the central sterile supply
options.D: Transfer the patient quickly to the recovery ward

explanation: An incorrect count requires an immediate stop to wound closure so that search efforts can begin while the field is still accessible. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT permissible when managing an unresolved needle count discrepancy?

options.A: Ordering an intraoperative X-ray to scan the surgical site
options.B: Searching the floor, trash cans, and sterile field thoroughly
options.C: Transferring the patient out of the operating room before imaging
options.D: Informing the lead surgeon of the missing item

explanation: Moving a patient with an unresolved count out of the theatre compromises safety and delays locating a potential retained item. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: How is an unrecorded surgical needle count viewed in a legal or malpractice investigation?
explanation: In legal contexts, if it is not documented, it is officially considered not done, leaving the facility vulnerable to liability. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: What specific detail must be included in the nursing documentation when a count discrepancy is initially found and subsequently resolved?

options.A: The personal phone number of the attending anesthetist
options.B: A clear note explaining the recount process and the resolution
options.C: Only the final successful count number without mentioning the error
options.D: A detailed financial estimate of the replacement surgical needle

explanation: Transparent documentation of discrepancies and how they were resolved provides a complete and legally defensible clinical record. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)
